# Results — Study 622 (Thematic-ETF-Curse)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test (Ben-David,
Franzoni, Kim & Moussawi, RFS 2023) — **specialized/thematic ETFs launch at peak hype and lose
about 5%/yr risk-adjusted over their first years; the launch date is the sell signal** —
rebuilt on a transparent panel of **48 thematic ETF launches (2005–2021)** with **13 broad
plain-vanilla index-ETF launches** as the placebo, SPY as the market and ^IRX as the risk-free.
Launch = the first candle on the tape (each ticker validated against the issuer's inception
month to guard against Yahoo ticker reuse). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `d3175d6dbc14`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return**) closes — 48 thematic ETFs + 13 broad index-ETF launches + SPY + ^IRX (public, no key) |
| Window | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30; thematic launches span **2005–2021** (20 of 48 in the 2018–2021 hype vintage) |
| Launch definition | first candle on the tape; ticker dropped if the first candle disagrees with the issuer's inception month by more than ~3 months (ticker-reuse guard — SPLG and ONLN fell to it) |
| CAPM | monthly excess-vs-excess: (fund − T-bill) on (SPY − T-bill); ^IRX level → monthly rf; alpha annualized ×12; **Newey-West t, lags = 6** (12 as robustness) |
| Execution / costs | membership (a fund's age) is public and known at month-end; positions form at the month-end close and hold the next month — **one lag everywhere** (the dip signal too); short overlay pays **5 bps one-way × NAV** + **borrow swept 300/600/1000 bps/yr** on the full short notional |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis — it works AGAINST the claim).** Delisted thematic
> ETFs — the worst bleeders, which shrank and closed (SNSR, YOLO, MOON, UFO, AWAY, NERD…) —
> return nothing on yfinance and are absent from the panel. Excluding the dead funds biases
> post-launch performance **up**, so the negative alpha below is an **understatement** of the
> category's curse. The bias strengthens, never manufactures, this finding.

## The signal — calendar-time "young thematics" portfolio, CAPM alpha vs SPY

Each month, equal-weight every thematic ETF within its first *W* **complete** months of life
(the partial launch month never enters; months with < 3 members are dropped). One time series →
CAPM regression → Newey-West *t* on the alpha. Calendar-time is the honest footing: pooled
fund-month regressions would count the same crash months dozens of times.

| portfolio | alpha (ann.) | HAC *t* | beta | months | avg members |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **young, first 36 months** | **−16.30%/yr** | **−3.27** | 1.64 | 192 (2008-07 → 2024-06) | 8.7 |
| young, first 12 months | −15.00%/yr | −2.04 | 1.64 | 109 (2008-07 → 2022-06) | 4.5 |
| seasoned (event months 37+) | −10.33%/yr | −1.82 | 1.36 | 182 | 23.6 |
| young − seasoned spread (beta-controlled) | −0.26%/yr | −0.05 | 0.20 | 158 | — |
| **placebo: broad-index launches, first 36 months** | **+0.31%/yr** | +1.17 | 0.99 | 72 | — |

The curse is **real and large**: the young-thematics book bleeds **−16.30%/yr** of CAPM alpha
at HAC *t* = **−3.27** — worse than Ben-David et al.'s ~−5%/yr, on a survivor-tilted panel that
should flatter it. The placebo is clean: broad-index launches show **no** post-launch drag
(+0.31%/yr, *t* = +1.17), so it is the *hype*, not the act of launching. One honest nuance,
said out loud: the **young-minus-seasoned spread alpha is ~0** (*t* = −0.05) — seasoned
thematics bleed too (−10.33%/yr, *t* = −1.82). The launch date *is* a sell signal in the
paper's sense (the bleed starts at the first candle), but the tape cannot certify that youth
is *extra* toxic relative to simply being a thematic.

## Event-time alpha curve — the bleed is steady, not front-loaded

Mean CAPM-abnormal return by event month (per-fund full-sample beta — a documented look-ahead
used for this descriptive curve only, never for the headline alpha), cumulated:

| event month | 12 | 24 | 36 | 48 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| cumulative abnormal | −4.9% | −12.4% | −22.5% | −35.6% |
| funds contributing | 48 | 48 | 48 | 48 |

## Per-fund view — why the calendar-time number is worse than the median fund

One first-36-months CAPM alpha per fund: median **−2.18%/yr**, **65%** of 48 funds negative.
The calendar-time alpha (−16.30%/yr) is far worse than the median fund because launches
**cluster** ahead of the theme's bust — the calendar months crowded with young funds (2008,
2021–22) were exactly the bleed months. That clustering *is* the paper's mechanism: issuers
launch when attention (and valuations) peak.

## Robustness

| variant | alpha (ann.) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| headline (W=36, lags=6, ≥3 members) | −16.30%/yr | −3.27 |
| NW lags = 12 | −16.30%/yr | −2.93 |
| min members = 1 (232 months) | −11.29%/yr | −2.32 |
| ex-ARK (42 funds) | −16.49%/yr | −3.34 |
| pre-2018 vintage (28 funds, 135 months) | −18.94%/yr | −3.99 |
| 2018+ vintage (20 funds, 74 months) | −9.56%/yr | −0.97 |

The headline survives the lag choice, the membership floor and dropping the entire ARK complex.
The 2018+ vintage alone does **not** clear (*t* = −0.97): its 74 calendar months are one
overlapping macro episode (2018→2024), so the sub-sample has little independent information —
named, not hidden. Both vintages carry the same sign.

## Tradability — the short survives modeled costs, then borrow reality bites

Short the young-thematics book, hedge with beta × SPY long, 5 bps one-way × NAV (entries/exits
amortized over the 36-month window), borrow paid on the **full** short notional:

| borrow (bps/yr) | net alpha (ann.) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| — gross | +16.30%/yr | +3.58 |
| 300 | **+13.21%/yr** | **+2.90** |
| 600 | +10.21%/yr | +2.24 |
| 1000 | +6.21%/yr | +1.37 |

The short clears the bar at textbook borrow (300–600 bps) — but the bleed is concentrated in
exactly the names whose borrow ran to double digits in the wild (cannabis, crypto-adjacent,
social-sentiment funds), availability on young niche ETFs is thin, and the squeeze risk on a
beta-1.6 short book is real. At 1000 bps the *t* dies. The retail-accessible implementation —
**refuse to buy launches** — is free but is an avoidance rule, not a return stream. FRAGILE.

## Third axis — does buying the −50% dip in a thematic work?

34 of 48 funds hit a −50% drawdown from their post-launch peak (month-end closes). Buy at the
**next** month's start (one lag), hold 36 months, calendar-time book:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| dip-buyer book CAPM alpha | **−19.39%/yr** · HAC *t* = **−2.80** (beta 1.63, 83 months) |
| forward 12m vs SPY | mean **−15.1 pp** (76% of 34 events negative) |
| forward 36m vs SPY | mean **−36.6 pp** (75% of 32 events negative) |

Down 50% is not cheap — it is mid-bleed. The dip-bought book loses alpha *faster* than the
young book itself, and three in four dips went on to lose to SPY over the next three years.
**BUSTED.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic seeded fund panel (staggered launches, beta ≈ 1.2) with a planted post-launch
alpha drag over event months 1–36:

| planted drag | recovered alpha | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0%/yr (null) | −0.76%/yr | −0.37 |
| −8%/yr | −8.76%/yr | −4.26 |

With no planted drag the pipeline does **not** manufacture a negative alpha; a planted −8%/yr
is recovered at −8.76%/yr. *(A machinery proof only — never cited in support of the stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The calendar-time young-thematics portfolio loses **−16.30%/yr** of CAPM
  alpha at HAC *t* = **−3.27** (W=12: −15.00%/yr, *t* = −2.04), robust to the lag choice
  (*t* = −2.93 at lags 12), the membership floor (*t* = −2.32) and dropping all of ARK
  (*t* = −3.34); the broad-launch placebo is clean (+0.31%/yr, *t* = +1.17); and the named
  **survivorship** bias (dead thematics missing) works **against** the finding. Nuance on the
  stamp: the young-vs-seasoned spread is ~0 — thematics bleed at every age; the launch is when
  the bleed *starts*, not a uniquely poisoned window.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The beta-hedged short nets **+13.2%/yr (t = 2.90)** at 5 bps +
  300 bps borrow and still clears at 600 bps — but the alpha lives in the very names with
  double-digit real-world borrow and thin availability, dies by 1000 bps (*t* = 1.37), and the
  free version (don't buy launches) isn't a return stream.
- **"Buy the −50% dip"? — BUSTED.** The dip-bought book bleeds **−19.39%/yr** of alpha
  (*t* = −2.80); the average dip went on to lose **36.6 pp** to SPY over three years, and 75%
  of the 32 events lost. The hype premium keeps bleeding below the halfway mark.
